admission.justification: Continuing in place and dropping the stop were weighed and rejected, and later work on roster continuation in the tree has to keep one read path, in which a kept family is continued by selecting it.

alternatives.option: At the end of the loaded members of a kept, partly loaded family, `j` stops at that family's continuation control with the usual message and loads nothing; using the control selects that family and continues its list.
alternatives.reason: The developer chose it (D36: "Stop at its control"). It keeps the stop that ICR-R32 rule 6 asks for at any family with unreturned members, and selecting the family is a request the server answers.

alternatives.option: Continue a kept family in place, without selecting it.
alternatives.reason: It needs a second read path and continues for a subject that is not selected.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The server continues a family's roster for a published cursor whatever subject is requested, so that a kept family can be continued without a second read path.

alternatives.option: No stop at the control of a kept family.
alternatives.reconsider_when: ICR-R32 rule 6 no longer requires that `j` stops at the continuation control of a family whose members are not all returned.

consequences: No selection and no key step loads a page of a kept family.
Continuing a kept family makes it the selected subject; the family that was selected before becomes a kept one.
The tree keeps the furthest cursor of two reads of one family, so the control continues where the furthest read ended.
context: A kept family can be one whose roster the server returned in part. Its continuation cursor was published for the subject it was read for, and the server offers a cursor only to the families of the requested subject's context (`family_context_cursor_refusal` in `mcp/src/agents_remember/application/review_family_rosters.py`). The question was what `j` does at the end of the returned members of such a family and how its roster continues.
